name: Autonomous Job Sourcing & Drafting Pipeline

parameters.text:
=Analyze the job posting provided below.

Your job is to extract and analyze information from the job posting and return ONLY the exact JSON schema provided.

JOB POSTING:

Job Title: {{ $json.job_title }}
Company: {{ $json.company }}
Source: {{ $json.source }}
Job URL: {{ $json.job_url }}
Description: {{ $json.description }}

Return ONLY valid JSON.

Use this exact schema:

{
  "required_skills": [],
  "experience_required": "",
  "employment_type": "",
  "location": "",
  "job_summary": "",
  "ai_automation_relevance": ""
}

Rules:

1. required_skills:
Extract the important skills explicitly required or preferred in the job description.

Include:
- Software and platforms
- Programming languages
- APIs
- AI tools
- Automation tools
- Workflow tools
- Marketing or business platforms
- Technical skills
- Other clearly relevant professional skills

Return an array of strings.

Do not invent skills that are not supported by the job description.

2. experience_required:
Extract the required or preferred experience from the job description.

Preserve the meaning and important details of the requirement.

If no experience requirement is stated, return "".

3. employment_type:
Extract the employment type stated in the job posting, such as:
- Full-time
- Part-time
- Contract
- Freelance
- Temporary
- Internship

If the job description does not clearly state it, return "".

4. location:
Extract the stated work location from the job posting.

If no location is stated, return "".

5. job_summary:
Write a concise summary describing what the person will actually do in the role.

Base this only on the job description.

6. ai_automation_relevance:
Analyze how relevant the job is to:
- Artificial intelligence
- AI tools
- Automation
- Workflow automation
- APIs
- AI agents
- Process automation
- Data automation
- AI-assisted workflows

Explain the relevance based ONLY on what is actually stated or clearly demonstrated by the job description.

If the role has little or no AI/automation relevance, say so clearly.

IMPORTANT:

- Return ONLY the JSON object.
- Do NOT use Markdown.
- Do NOT use ```json code fences.
- Do NOT calculate Job Score.
- Do NOT calculate Recommendation.
- Do NOT return job_score.
- Do NOT return recommendation.
- Do NOT return skill_score.
- Do NOT return relevance_score.
- Do NOT return remote_score.
- Do NOT return matched_skills.
- Do NOT invent information.
- Do NOT infer requirements that are not supported by the job posting.
- Do NOT add fields outside the exact schema.

parameters.jsCode:
return items.map(item => {
  const job = item.json.jobs || {};

  return {
    json: {
      job_id: job.id || "",
      job_title: job.title || "",
      company: job.company || "",

      job_url: job.job_url || "",
      job_url_direct: job.job_url_direct || "",

      source: job.site || "",
      description: job.description || "",
      date_posted: job.date_posted || "",

      employment_type: job.job_type || "",
      remote: job.is_remote === true,
      location: job.location || "",

      salary: {
        source: job.salary_source || "",
        min: job.min_amount ?? null,
        max: job.max_amount ?? null,
        currency: job.currency || "",
        interval: job.interval || ""
      },

      job_level: job.job_level || "",
      job_function: job.job_function || "",
      listing_type: job.listing_type || "",

      emails: job.emails ?? null,

      company_industry: job.company_industry ?? null,
      company_description: job.company_description ?? null,

      skills: job.skills ?? null,
      experience_range: job.experience_range ?? null,

      company_rating: job.company_rating ?? null,
      company_reviews_count: job.company_reviews_count ?? null,
      vacancy_count: job.vacancy_count ?? null,

      work_from_home_type: job.work_from_home_type ?? null,

      jobspy_raw: job
    }
  };
});
